feature: CCNA Switching: STP Root Bridge Selection

topology.SW1: Bridge MAC 0200.0000.0030; target VLAN 10 primary/base priority 24576; Gi0/24 to SW2 and Gi0/23 to SW3
topology.SW2: Bridge MAC 0200.0000.0020; target VLAN 10 secondary/base priority 28672; Gi0/24 to SW1, Gi0/23 to SW3, Gi0/1 to PC1
topology.SW3: Bridge MAC 0200.0000.0010; VLAN 10 default/base priority 32768; Gi0/23 to SW1, Gi0/24 to SW2, Gi0/1 to PC2
topology.Initial election: All priorities are 32768; SW3 wins because it has the lowest bridge MAC

checks: Independent portable attempts begin with zero credit, fixed bridge identities, equal VLAN 10 priorities, a real lowest-MAC SW3 election and already-working same-VLAN traffic; connectivity alone earns only traffic/learning observations
Published IOS reference commands select higher-MAC SW1 through lower priority, configure SW2 secondary, retain SW3 default and save all three startup configurations
Five configured/elected port-role tasks pass before actual traffic; dynamic MAC learning and two observed PC directions complete all eight tasks
Equal bridge priorities at 0, 24576 and 32768 select the lowest bridge MAC; the guide tie experiment restores all-default priorities and demonstrates SW3 taking the root again
Bridge priority is compared before MAC; changing a port MAC or hostname does not replace the fixed bridge identity
Actual delivered BPDUs are required for root agreement and expected non-root port-role credit; accepted priorities alone cannot impersonate a complete election
Secondary SW2 takes over when primary SW1 powers off while both surviving PCs stay reachable; saved lower primary priority reclaims the root after recovery
Isolating a powered SW1 creates separate components: SW1 remains its own root while SW2/SW3 elect SW2; reconnecting the trunks reunites the intended election
A root-uplink failure changes the path through SW3 while preserving SW1 as root and retaining both PC directions
A per-interface VLAN cost override changes SW3 root port to Gi0/24 without changing its elected root bridge; removing the override restores the intended role goal
A later superior priority can win because root macros are one-time settings; restoring that bridge default recovers the intended primary without dynamic root-defense behavior
Actual tagged Layer 2 ICMP frames use the elected tree without TTL loss; the alternate port does not transmit user packets. Dynamic MAC clear removes learning credit until new ingress traffic arrives
All published show/ping commands work; Root ID and Bridge ID expose actual MACs, displayed priorities 24586/28682/32778 including VLAN 10 system ID, and the intended Root FWD/Desg FWD/Altn BLK roles
Portable saves, renamed nodes and startup power cycles retain fixed identities, priorities and earned echoes while elections and dynamic MAC state rebuild
The guide includes an escaped custom comparison-table caption; existing labs retain the default Addressing plan caption and all original catalog workflows
